stats.label: AI use cases coached to production

caseStudies.name: Smart Self-Improving Lines: turning one-off AI wins into repeatable playbooks
caseStudies.metricLabel: proven solutions in reapplication (filling, labelling, capping)
caseStudies.role: Drove the concept end-to-end: defined the Common Best Approach, aligned business and technical stakeholders, and partnered with sites to select lead and demo lines.
caseStudies.problem: Successful manufacturing AI pilots existed, but scaling them to other lines and sites depended on knowledge held by a few people: technical know-how, infrastructure readiness, configuration details and deployment steps. We started with the problems behind the largest share of scrap, such as filling and labelling.
caseStudies.action: Developed the Common Best Approach (CBA) concept to capture proven solutions end-to-end for reapplication, and structured technical readiness around SmartBox, AI Inference Server, GitHub, connectivity, automation-platform requirements, ownership and site roles. Introduced AI agents to document solutions and generate step-by-step workflows for repeatable tasks, so the playbook improves with every deployment. Collaborated with business and site stakeholders to identify lead and demo sites that prove a solution delivers value beyond its original line.
caseStudies.result: Established a reusable path from successful pilot → documented standard → demonstration site → broader scale. Perfect Fill and the PE labeler became the first concrete applications of the approach, with cappers next.
caseStudies.learning: A pilot isn't a product until someone else can run it without you. Write the playbook while the knowledge is still fresh.

caseStudies.name: Anomaly detection: catching the failures you have never seen
caseStudies.metricLabel: use cases running on one standard approach
caseStudies.role: Owned the deployment approach end-to-end and coached site project teams, collaborating with maintenance, quality and engineering stakeholders while sites built and ran their own projects.
caseStudies.problem: Unplanned stops were costing production time, and there was no standard way to detect anomalies across many signals and processes. Predictive models hit a basic blocker: failures are rare, so there were never enough labelled examples to train a supervised model.
caseStudies.action: Standardised on an off-the-shelf anomaly-detection app on Siemens Industrial Edge built on unsupervised models. Instead of learning what a failure looks like, it learns what normal looks like, so it can flag unforeseen and rare, high-impact events without labelled failure data, making it a practical starting point for any line. Drove adoption by partnering with site teams on each pilot and turning every success into a reusable, scalable deployment pattern.
caseStudies.result: Piloted first on a one-off breakage that had cost millions: the model surfaced the failure in the data, and an induced-failure test confirmed it. The next use case was a frequent defect in moulding, where the model raised accurate alerts within one day of deployment, which won the teams' confidence. It now runs across 15 use cases.
caseStudies.learning: When failures are rare, stop waiting for labels. Teach the model what normal looks like and let it tell you when something isn't.

caseStudies.name: AI-X: removing the entry barrier from model to machine
caseStudies.role: Conceived, built and owned AI-X as an internal product end-to-end, from first prototype on a production line to the standard packaging route; worked with business stakeholders and IT to drive adoption.
caseStudies.problem: Building an ML model was never the slow part; getting it onto the machine was. Every model had to be hand-fitted to the Siemens Industrial Edge SDK, which took as long as developing it, and the work came back after every retrain. Deployments slipped and adoption stalled.
caseStudies.action: Mapped exactly which parts of the SDK change from model to model and built a model-agnostic skeleton around them. Engineers describe their Python ML model in a few text inputs and a CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions produces the deployment package end-to-end. Applied DevOps practices throughout: pytest unit tests, standard pre- and post-processing quality gates, SonarQube scans for IT compliance, application registration, and built-in tracking of performance, usage and user reception. Collaborated with IT, site engineers and data scientists to make it the default route.
caseStudies.result: A stable production solution that now packages most of the models we deploy to the edge. Retraining no longer means a new deployment project: updates ship through the same pipeline, cutting time-to-production and lowering the entry barrier for new teams.
caseStudies.learning: Automate the part everyone repeats, not the part everyone notices.

caseStudies.name: WISE Coach Qualification (WCQ): the real power is people
caseStudies.role: Program lead: shaped the regional technical qualification, designed the learning journeys and facilitated sessions across regions.
caseStudies.problem: Scaling manufacturing AI needs people across regions who can spot valuable use cases, understand the architecture and tools, and support deployment, not just a central technical team. Great solutions only create value when people adopt and use them, so investing in capability is how AI delivers business results.
caseStudies.action: Helped structure the regional WISE technical qualification and training. Mapped participant capability across Python, JMP and SmartBox, and built the learning journey around architecture, SmartBox, anomaly detection, hands-on tool usage and use-case/MVP development. Adapted delivery to regional availability and mixed skill levels, collaborating with regional leads and subject-matter experts.
caseStudies.result: Created a practical capability-building approach that works for coders and non-coders alike, using tools such as JMP, and tied training directly to real manufacturing use cases and MVPs instead of theory. The program has supported 55+ coached use cases across 11+ business units.
caseStudies.learning: Learning sticks when it ships. Tie every cohort to a production problem with an owner.

caseStudies.name: Touchless quality: replacing manual sampling
caseStudies.role: Set up the ML approach and led cross-functional alignment with the quality organisation, delivered together with site and data teams.
caseStudies.problem: Product quality was checked through manual sampling — slow, labour-intensive and blind between samples.
caseStudies.action: Drove a cloud ML approach for continuous quality prediction end-to-end, from data to model to acceptance, and partnered with the quality organisation and site teams to define validation and acceptance criteria.
caseStudies.result: Secured quality-organisation acceptance for scale-up, with ~$12M of identified opportunity across further lines.
caseStudies.learning: In regulated domains the hardest part is trust. Bring the quality team in at the start, not at sign-off.

caseStudyNote: Dollar values are rounded estimates from internal business cases, not audited savings. "Identified opportunity" means potential value across further sites, not realised value. Results are team outcomes; my role is stated on each case. Details are kept at a level that respects confidentiality.

featuredProject.name: Coinfluence
featuredProject.summary: A personal finance dashboard I designed and built for my household. It reads monthly exports from six German banks and brokers and answers three questions: how much did we spend, how much did we save and invest, and who owes whom on the shared card.
features: One upload for every bank: the account is detected and duplicates are skipped
Swipe deck to split shared credit-card charges, with a settle-up checklist
Budgets, recurring-payment detection and net worth over time
Two profiles with separate data and settings

decisions.title: Local-first by design
decisions.text: Financial data never leaves the laptop; sync goes only to a private repo, and the sync script refuses to run on a public one.

decisions.title: Trust over features
decisions.text: Automatic backups before every save, file locking, and damaged files are never overwritten.

decisions.title: Tested without real data
decisions.text: The test suite builds fake statements for every bank, and CI runs it on every push.

featuredProject.note: The source is private because it handles personal financial data. Happy to demo it live.

aboutMe:
I was a 90s kid who grew up watching science fiction, fascinated by worlds where technology could do things that seemed impossible. I’ve always loved the idea of what could be—and the curiosity to figure out how to make it happen. Looking back, perhaps it’s no surprise that I found my way into IT, AI, and innovation. Today, I get to bring a little of that futuristic thinking into the real world.

At Procter & Gamble’s Kronberg Innovation Center, I lead the scaling of manufacturing AI across a global plant network—connecting factory-floor challenges with data science, IT, and engineering to turn promising pilots into solutions that work in production.

I’m fascinated by the technology, but even more by what makes innovation stick: solving the right problems, building reusable solutions, bringing cross-functional teams together, and empowering people to carry ideas forward themselves.

Beyond technology, I’m a curious lifelong learner who enjoys teaching, building teams, and turning ambitious goals into tangible results.

I’m a planner with a bias for action. I like turning ideas into plans and plans into progress. But life rarely follows a perfect roadmap. When things don’t go to plan, I adapt, learn, and keep moving. I’m an optimist about detours; sometimes, what feels like a setback leads somewhere even better than we had imagined.

I’m also a strategic thinker who likes to roll up my sleeves and get things done. I enjoy seeing the bigger picture while figuring out the practical steps to make it happen. And I believe the best ideas rarely succeed in isolation—they need people who challenge one another, share knowledge, and bring out the best in each other. For me, that’s where strategy turns into progress: when good ideas meet good people and the willingness to make things happen.
